## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Anonymous for authors: authors upload an anonymised manuscript with no title page and a separate title page, and the guidelines say "ASR uses anonymous peer reviewers" (https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr, copy dated 2025-07-18). Whether reviewers' identities are also hidden from authors is implied by that wording; no separate statement. An editor screens first: 337 of 631 new submissions in 2025 were rejected after internal review (editors' report, ASA page copy dated 2026-06-30) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. The guidelines page text (copy dated 2025-07-18) contains no transfer or cascade wording (searched for "transfer" and "cascade": 0 hits). ASR does not consider submissions of papers previously rejected at ASR (same page) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | 2025 (editors' report, https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/, copy dated 2026-06-30): of 294 new submissions sent for review, 52 (18%) received an invitation to revise, 220 (75%) were rejected and 1 was accepted; of 73 revised manuscripts received, 29% were conditionally accepted, 45% accepted outright, 11% got another R&R and 10% were rejected; none of the 31 papers invited to a second or later round was rejected. SciRev (16 reviews): 1.3 review rounds on average, 2.9 review reports on average (https://scirev.org/journal/american-sociological-review/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. The Sage home page links reviewer guidelines with separate sets for general, comparative-historical, qualitative, policy, theoretical and experimental work (https://web.archive.org/web/20260514121133/https://journals.sagepub.com/home/asr, copy dated 2026-05-14); the guideline pages themselves were not read (no archived copy found) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific text found. The guidelines page (copy dated 2025-07-18) contains no mention of artificial intelligence or generative tools (0 hits outside HTML comments). The editors' 2025 report says the editors had spent time with the board on generative-AI questions and were waiting for an official ASA AI policy (https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/, copy dated 2026-06-30). The publisher-wide Sage policy applies |

| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with disclosure for generative content; same rubric as other entries in this corpus) |
| **Summary** | Sage policy (copy dated 2024-12-13): assistive AI that improves language, grammar or structure needs no disclosure; tools that produce text, references, images or other content must be disclosed, naming the model and purpose in the methods or acknowledgements; AI cannot be an author; authors must verify generated content and citations; undisclosed inappropriate use can lead to rejection at any stage. Reviewers and editors may not use generative AI to write reports or decision letters. This is an older copy; the current policy may differ |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20241213223927/https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/chatgpt-and-generative-ai (Sage policy, copy dated 2024-12-13); https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/ (editors' remark on a pending ASA policy) |

### Preprint Policy

> ASA-level policy for all ASA journals ("Green Open Access"), page last updated 2022-09-21, copy dated 2026-01-01: https://web.archive.org/web/20260101010622/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/online-posting-policy/. The ASR guidelines page itself says nothing about preprints (searched, 0 hits).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | Authors may share the version submitted to the journal anywhere at any time |
| Under review | Yes | Same rule, since it covers the submitted version. The guidelines call simultaneous submission to another journal unethical (https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr). A posted preprint can weaken the anonymised review the journal asks for; the pages do not address this |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes | Accepted version may go on a personal or department site, an institutional or subject repository, without restriction or embargo. Embargo: none stated |
| Version of Record | Not without permission | Published version may not be posted on a website or repository without ASA or publisher permission; teaching use, supply to colleagues, and use in a book the author alone writes or edits are allowed |

## Format

> Source: ASR guidelines page, Wayback copy dated 2025-07-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr. The page's HTML comments (cookie banners and layout notes) were excluded. Anything newer than that date is unverified.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Articles and Comments/Replies (the guidelines give separate limits for both). The ASA page says the journal does not publish book reviews (https://web.archive.org/web/20261025195354/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/american-sociological-review/, copy dated 2026-10-25). The editors say papers "tend to combine very strong research designs and analytic methods" with general-interest framing and theory development (guidelines page, "What we publish") |
| **Word limit** | Articles may not exceed 15,000 words including text, references and footnotes, excluding tables and figures; Comments/Replies 3,000 words (guidelines, copy dated 2025-07-18) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The page states the limit as a maximum and says nothing on exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | The submission step asks for an abstract of 200 words or fewer; the manuscript-preparation section says 150 to 200 words, no identifying information; four or five keywords go on the title page (same page; the two abstract figures differ) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap. References count inside the 15,000 words. All authors must be listed, "et al." is not acceptable in the reference list, and dataset references should carry a persistent identifier such as a DOI. Notes should not exceed 100 words each |
| **Supplementary material** | Blank. The page text contains no supplementary-material section (searched for "supplement": 0 hits); appendixes are allowed and should be lettered |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables and figures are numbered consecutively with titles; significance stars follow p < .05, .01, .001 and one- or two-tailed tests must be named; permission for reproduced material must be supplied |
| **Style / submission format** | Double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman, margins of at least one inch, no page numbers; submission through Sage Track with a cover letter, abstract, title page and anonymised manuscript; author-year citations in ASA style (the page refers to the ASA Style Guide, 7th ed., 2022); ORCID collected from the corresponding author |

### Orientation

> Counts come from Crossref records of the journal dated 2021-01-11 to 2026-11-21: 237 journal-article records, 220 with an abstract (92.8%). A record counts when its title or abstract matches the regular expression listed in the AI-Research Notes (case-insensitive, word-bounded). Shares use the 220 records with abstracts as denominator; counts are lower bounds. Retrieved 2026-11-23, source https://api.crossref.org/journals/0003-1224/works.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Mostly empirical by method words: "survey" 38 (17.3%), "interview" 42 (19.1%), "panel/longitudinal" 20 (9.1%), "experiment" 19 (8.6%), "historical/archival" 23 (10.5%), against "conceptual" 4 (1.8%). "theory" appears in 77 abstracts (35.0%), but the word is also used in empirical framing, so it does not identify purely theoretical papers. The editors name "new theoretical developments" among the journal's aims (ASA page, copy dated 2026-10-25) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Both present. Quantitative words: "survey" 17.3%, "regression" 5.0%, "quantitative" 2.7%, "causal" 3.2%. Qualitative words: "interview" 19.1%, "ethnograph-" 6.8%, "qualitative" 4.5%, "participant observation/fieldwork" 2.7%. "mixed methods" 3.2%. Counts cannot say which design is the larger share of papers, because a survey experiment or an interview-based study may use none of these words |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Not scored from counts. The aims text welcomes "all areas of sociology" with emphasis on "general interest" (Sage page, copy dated 2026-05-14; the same wording is on the older Sage journal-description page, https://web.archive.org/web/20211030id_/https://journals.sagepub.com/description/asr, copy dated 2021-10-30, read 2026-11-23). Topic words in abstracts: "race/racism" 17.3%, "gender" 15.0%, "inequality" 25.9%, "organizations/firms/labor market" 24.5%, "states/politics" 41.8% (broad regex, see notes) |

| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries on the 223 OpenAlex articles dated 2021-2026 (articles with at least one author in the country): United States 191, United Kingdom 15, Canada 14, Germany 9, France 8, Italy 8, Netherlands 6, United Arab Emirates 4, Israel 4, Norway 4 (OpenAlex works API group_by authorships.countries, retrieved 2026-11-23). The editors' 2025 report says many submissions still come from elite institutions and that the board is discussing ways to extend the journal's global reach; almost one quarter of reviewers are outside the United States (https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/, copy dated 2026-06-30) |

Detail in Reviewer Pool Characteristics |

The editors' report says it is important to tell potential authors that ASR waives submission fees for authors in low-income countries (ASA page copy dated 2026-06-30). No statement on non-Western epistemologies found |

The editors' 2025 report describes board composition (61 percent women, 5 percent gender queer or gender nonconforming, 52 percent members of a racial or ethnic minority group) and a goal that underrepresented groups see themselves as potential authors and reviewers (ASA page copy dated 2026-06-30). That is a statement about people, not about topic acceptance |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No single school dominates by named thinkers in 220 abstracts: Bourdieu 3, Weber 3, Durkheim 2, Marx 1, Foucault 1, Goffman 2; "intersectional" 6 (2.7%), "institutional theory/neo-institutional" 5 (2.3%), "world-systems/world society" 4 (1.8%), "life course" 5 (2.3%), "social capital" 5 (2.3%). "critical race / racialized organizations" 2 (0.9%), though one of the page's most-read articles is "A Theory of Racialized Organizations" (Sage page copy dated 2026-05-14). The most-cited 2021-2026 records in Crossref (citation counts as of retrieval) are on statistical estimands and theory (338; https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224211004187), platform architecture and contention in China (208; https://doi.org/10.1177/0003122420979980), the wealth inequality of nations (197; https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224211027800), cultural schemas (159; https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224211024525) and algorithmic and in-person screening in housing discrimination (158; https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224211029618). The journal states no political position on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One stated criterion: when deciding whether to send a paper out for review, the editors say they apply three criteria, "quality of methods, general sociological appeal, and breadth" (guidelines page "What we publish", https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr, copy dated 2025-07-18). The ASA page repeats that all areas of sociology are welcome, "with emphasis on exceptional quality and general interest" (copy dated 2026-10-25).
- **What kind of engagement?** The guidelines say papers "tend to combine very strong research designs and analytic methods, general interest framing, and theory development that transcends subfields" and advise reading recent articles to see this. The ASA page lists "original works", "new theoretical developments", research that advances understanding of "fundamental social processes", and "important methodological innovations" as the mission (https://web.archive.org/web/20261025195354/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/american-sociological-review/, copy dated 2026-10-25).
- **Article type and length**: articles up to 15,000 words including references; Comments/Replies up to 3,000 words; no book reviews (https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr, copy dated 2025-07-18; see Format).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the 2025 data show the outcome in aggregate: 337 of 631 new submissions (53%) were rejected after internal review and not sent out (editors' report, https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/, copy dated 2026-06-30). Reasons for individual desk rejections are blank: the report does not give them.
- **Special-issue framing seen**: none. No call for papers found on the pages read.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-11 to 2026-11-21 whose title or abstract matches the regex listed in the AI-Research Notes; the denominator is the 220 records with an abstract (237 records in all; counts are lower bounds). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. The scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written for psychology and the humanities; where a row does not fit sociology it says so, and four rows were added.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | "experiment" 19 (8.6%), but the word includes survey and field experiments and does not separate laboratory work; "causal" 7 (3.2%) |
| Quantitative survey / observational (added row) | 3 | "survey" 38 (17.3%), "panel/longitudinal" 20 (9.1%), "regression" 11 (5.0%), "administrative data/register/census" 10 (4.5%), "quantitative" 6 (2.7%). The editors name "quality of methods" as a screening criterion and the reviewer guidelines list separate sets for general, experimental and policy work (Sage page copy dated 2026-05-14, guideline pages unread) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 42 (19.1%), "qualitative" 10 (4.5%) |
| Ethnography and fieldwork (added row) | 3 | "ethnograph-" 15 (6.8%), "participant observation/fieldwork" 6 (2.7%); the Sage page lists a separate qualitative reviewer-guideline set |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 220 abstracts. The row is a poor fit for this venue: no sociology-specific evidence was sought beyond the count |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | By the convention, "theory" 77 (35.0%) scores 3, but that overstates pure theory work because the word appears in empirical framing; "conceptual" alone 4 (1.8%) would score 2. The ASA page names "new theoretical developments" in the mission and the Sage page lists a theoretical reviewer-guideline set. Treat as 2-3 |
| Mixed methods | 2 | "mixed methods" 7 (3.2%) |
| Comparative-historical / archival (added row) | 3 | "historical/archival" 23 (10.5%, includes papers that merely cover historical periods), "comparative-historical" 2 (0.9%); the Sage page lists a comparative-historical reviewer-guideline set |
| Computational / text-as-data (added row) | 3 | "computational/text/ML" 12 (5.5%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | "meta-analysis" 1 (0.5%), "systematic review" 0. The row is a poor fit for this venue and is not evidence of rejection |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. In the 220 abstracts (abstract-only text; the counts do not cover titles or full text), 212 (96.4%) contain I, my, we or our (capitalised forms included); 147 contain "we" or "We"; 70 contain "I" or "my" (Crossref, regexes in notes; "our" can also be a generic plural, so this measures first-person wording, not necessarily a single author's voice). Examples seen in the first 260 characters of recent abstracts: "We first distinguish..." (https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224261500693), "we use a novel survey experiment" (https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224261486015); impersonal openings: "This article examines..." (https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224261489725), "This article introduces..." (https://doi.org/10.1177/00031224261475238). The guidelines only ask authors to cite their own work in the third person for anonymity ("Smith (1992) concluded...", not "I concluded (Smith 1992)") |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 15,000 words including references and footnotes; notes up to 100 words each (guidelines, copy dated 2025-07-18). No page-length statistics were taken |
| **Abstract and keywords** | 200 words or fewer at submission and 150 to 200 words in the manuscript-preparation section; four or five keywords on the title page (same page) |
| **Writing style notes** | ASA style, author-year citations with page numbers after a colon, three heading levels generally enough, notes numbered with superscripts, all authors listed in references; "Cite only those works needed to provide evidence" (guidelines page). The editors advise reading recent ASR articles to see the expected combination of design, framing and theory |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author counts over 237 records (2021-2026): 82 single-author, 69 two authors, 44 three, 13 four, 5 five, 5 six, one each with 7, 8 and 9, one record with 158 listed authors, and 15 records with no author list (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0003-1224/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Editors: 4 sociologists at the University of Massachusetts-Amherst (term 2024-2028 per the ASA page). The 2025 report says the board had 5 deputy editors and 61 regular members, and that 1,055 scholars from around the world reviewed for ASR between 2025-01-01 and 2026-05-05, 213 of them more than once; almost one quarter are outside the United States. The report also says reviewers' work "most of that work ultimately appears in other journals" (quoted) | https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/ ; https://web.archive.org/web/20261025195354/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/american-sociological-review/ |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank for individual behaviour. One author-reported SciRev data point: reviewer comments rated 4.0 of 5 for difficulty and review reports 3.7 of 5 for quality, from 16 reviews (https://scirev.org/journal/american-sociological-review/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The editors report that some reviewers accept and never deliver, and that more potential reviewers do not reply (editors' report, copy dated 2026-06-30) | SciRev; editors' report |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No source. Both interview-based and survey-based work are common in abstracts (see Methodological Preferences); that does not show how reviewers treat qualitative work | Crossref counts |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | Board page (copy dated 2026-08-24), 70 entries: 4 editors, 5 deputy editors, 61 board members. By country as printed: USA 55 (the count includes one board member at a university in Lebanon whose country is printed as USA), Canada 4, UK 2, Chile 1, Spain 1, Taiwan 1, South Korea 1, South Africa 1, France 1, China 1 (Hong Kong university), Germany 1, no country printed 1; 55+4+2+1+1+1+1+1+1+1+1+1 = 70. Editors and deputy editors: 9 of 9 at US institutions. One board member is at a community college | https://web.archive.org/web/20260824142116/https://journals.sagepub.com/editorial-board/asr |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No IRB or ethics-approval statement on the guidelines page (searched for "IRB", "institutional review", "informed consent", "human subjects": 0 hits). The page requires authors to follow ASA guidelines and the ASA Code of Ethics on plagiarism and other ethical issues, and says submission to another journal while under review at ASR is regarded as unethical (https://web.archive.org/web/20250718052929/https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/asr, copy dated 2025-07-18) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are common: 82 of the 222 Crossref records that list authors for 2021-2026 (37%; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0003-1224/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The title page asks for institutional affiliations; no independent-scholar rule found (guidelines copy dated 2025-07-18). The editors say many submissions come from elite institutions with larger research budgets (editors' report, copy dated 2026-06-30). The 25 dollar fee is waived for ASA student members; fee waivers for authors in low-income countries are described in the editors' report |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The guidelines say authors must adhere to the ASA data-sharing policy (share data "as a regular practice", with exceptions for proprietary agreements and for confidentiality that cannot be protected). The editors report that 28 percent of papers made data and code available in 2023, 47 percent in 2025 with a further 12 percent on request, and 82 percent of 2026 articles as of April provide data, code or interview schedules; they say they urge accepted authors to do this (editors' report, https://web.archive.org/web/20260630134016/https://www.asanet.org/publications/journals/annual-reports/, copy dated 2026-06-30) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Authors upload an anonymised manuscript with no title page and a separate identifying title page (guidelines, copy dated 2025-07-18). The ASA policy allows the submitted version to be posted anywhere at any time, so a preprint is permitted although it can reveal authorship to reviewers (policy copy dated 2026-01-01) |
| **AI use** | See AI Policy: Sage policy requires disclosure of generative content; no journal-specific text found |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; 25 dollar submission fee; APC unverified (OpenAlex lists 3900 dollars); see Open Access |
| **Originality screening** | The guidelines name plagiarism under ASA ethics rules but describe no similarity-check step (searched for "similarity": 0 hits) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: articles may not exceed 15,000 words including text, references and footnotes, and Comments/Replies 3,000 (Format; guidelines copy dated 2025-07-18).
- **Anonymisation**: the manuscript must carry no title page and no identifying wording; self-citation must be in the third person (Format; Voice & Style).
- **Prior rejection at ASR**: ASR does not consider submissions of papers previously rejected at the journal (Peer Review; guidelines copy dated 2025-07-18).
- **Simultaneous submission**: submitting to another journal while under review at ASR is regarded as unethical (Practical Concerns, IRB row).
- **Submission fee**: 25 dollars, non-refundable, for all new manuscripts unless authored by ASA student members (Open Access, APC row).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; the live guidelines page could not be read directly and the 2025-07-18 copy may be out of date.

### Soft Tax

- **Selectivity**: the editors' 2025 report gives a 4.8% acceptance rate and 337 of 631 new submissions (53%) rejected after internal review (Metrics, Desk Rejection Rate and Acceptance Rate rows). Each new submission therefore faces a first screen before any reviewer sees it.
- **Time**: 6.8 weeks average to decision for new submissions and 13.2 weeks for peer-reviewed ones in 2025 (Review Cycle Time); SciRev authors report 7.1 months total handling for accepted manuscripts (16 reviews, author-reported, unverified).
- **Bar on framing**: the editors screen for "quality of methods, general sociological appeal, and breadth" (Framing Requirements). A paper aimed at one sub-field only is outside the stated emphasis on "general interest"; the page does not say such papers are rejected.
- **Data and code**: the editors ask accepted authors to make data, code or interview schedules public, and 82 percent of 2026 articles had done so as of April (Practical Concerns, Data transparency row). This is a request, not a stated rule.
- **Reviewer difficulty (author-reported)**: SciRev lists reviewer-comment difficulty 4.0 of 5 from 16 reviews (Reviewer Pool Characteristics).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical sociology with a strong design and a framing that reaches beyond one sub-field: the stated screening criteria (Framing Requirements) and counts of "survey" 17.3%, "interview" 19.1%, "panel/longitudinal" 9.1% in abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Interview- or ethnography-based qualitative work with a general argument: "interview" 19.1% and "ethnograph-" 6.8% of abstracts, and the Sage page lists a separate qualitative reviewer-guideline set (Methodological Preferences).
- Work on stratification, race, gender, organizations or politics: "inequality" 25.9%, "race/racism" 17.3%, "gender" 15.0%, "organizations/firms/labor market" 24.5% of abstracts (Orientation, Sensitive Topics).
- Authors who can share data and code: 47 percent of 2025 authors did, 82 percent of 2026 articles by April (Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers needing a fast, near-certain outcome: 4.8% acceptance rate (Metrics) and a 53% internal-review rejection share in 2025 (Metrics).
- Pure book reviews: the ASA page says the journal does not publish book reviews (Format).
- Work in autoethnography or systematic review: 0 of 220 abstracts match either (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these forms are absent, not that they are rejected.
- Authors who cannot anonymise: the journal requires an anonymised manuscript (Hard Blockers).
- Anyone needing a confirmed APC: the amount (3900 dollars) is only an OpenAlex listing (Open Access).
